\# Why 30M and 1H, Not 15M

← [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]]

## The rule

Stick to the **30-minute and 1-hour** charts for aligning a swing to a [[4H Profiling|4H profile]]. Avoid using the 15-minute chart for this purpose.

## Why

Dropping to the 15-minute chart tends to produce noise — you start finding a random swing here, a random swing there, and end up confusing yourself rather than getting a cleaner read. The 30M/1H charts are described as the highest-probability timeframes for this specific alignment task.

## The narrow exception

[[90-Minute Cracking Correlation]] intentionally goes *past* 15M down to a 5-minute or 3-minute chart for execution — but only as a last resort when there is no gap anywhere on the 4H, 1H, or 30M, and no [[Regular Swing Point Rule (Only Inside C2)|C2 swing point]] available either. That's a deliberate, narrow fallback, not a reason to default to lower timeframes generally.

## Related
- [[The Wick-in-Gap Alignment Setup]]
- [[Example 7 - Continuation Equal Highs 1H Swing in Gap]] — closing example explicitly reinforcing this preference

\# Example 1 — RTY/YM, 6AM Reversal, 1H Gap

← [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]] · Concept: [[The Wick-in-Gap Alignment Setup]]

## 4H setup

A 06:00 reversal, with SMT at the highs. The key level is a previous day high that lines up with another prior high — a valid key level for the reversal. This is a [[4H Profiling|4H profile]] [[0600 Reversal]] setup, expecting **10:00 continuation**.

## Lower-timeframe alignment

Dropped to the **1-hour chart**: the SMT high (the rejection point) is visible, along with a gap. 10:00 opens above that gap. A 30-minute gap is present, and since the 1-hour candle also closed, it forms a 1-hour gap as well. The plan: wait for price to trade into that gap and reverse away from it.

## Cross-asset confirmation

Checked **RTY vs. YM** — same setup, same 1-hour gap, with SMT between the two. Both are looking for 10:00 continuation, and it doesn't matter which of the two you'd actually trade — RTY has a clear draw on liquidity at a low, and YM shares the same 1-hour gap structure.

## The entry

At **11:00 AM**, price taps into the gap with SMT confirming — that's the aligned 1-hour swing point. RTY reaches its draw on liquidity; YM reaches its own lower target.

## Takeaway

A clean, textbook version of [[The Wick-in-Gap Alignment Setup]]: 4H reversal with SMT → 1H gap identified → cross-checked on a correlated asset → SMT confirms the tap into the gap → continuation trade to the draw.

\# Example 2 — C3 Creates Its Own Key Level

← [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]] · Concept: [[The Wick-in-Gap Alignment Setup]]

## 4H setup

A C3 continuation scenario with an external draw above, after internal range liquidity was hit. C2 had SMT at a low and put in a valid reversal. The plan: C3 should open and tap a key level within itself to trade higher.

## The wrinkle: C2 left no key level

Dropped to the **30-minute chart**: there was already an existing swing point, and 06:00 opened and expanded away without leaving a gap. Since C2 didn't leave a usable key level, the rule shifts: **let C3 create its own key level** (a gap) instead.

## Waiting for confirmation

C3 puts in its own gap to reverse off of, but there's **no SMT inside that gap yet**. Rather than force it, the plan is to let that candle close and let the **next candle** provide the SMT.

On the following candle: SMT confirms between two correlated assets — one asset (RB) takes out this candle's low while the other doesn't. That's the entry — position to trade toward the external high.

## Takeaway

When C2 doesn't leave a key level of its own, C3 can generate one instead. If SMT isn't present inside that gap immediately, it's acceptable to wait one more candle for the SMT to confirm rather than forcing the entry — the same patience principle as [[SMT Confirmation Rule]] from [[4H Profiling]], applied at the lower-timeframe alignment layer. Also confirmed as an hourly SMT on zoom-out, though the 30-minute gap was preferred for entry — consistent with [[Why 30M and 1H, Not 15M]].

## Related
- [[The Wick-in-Gap Alignment Setup]]
- [[Two-Stage SMT for the Reversal Candle]]

\# Example 3 — Simultaneous C3 Opens, EQ Reversal

← [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]] · Concept: [[Simultaneous C3 Across Timeframes (No Swing Forms)]]

## Setup

10:00 opens and **expands away immediately**, without ever forming a 1-hour or 30-minute swing to wait for.

## How this was anticipated

- SMT was already present between two candles, alongside a heavy prior displacement lower.
- Measured the **EQ (equilibrium / 50%)** of the entire prior range (from the swing low up to the swing high). The plan: expect the new candle's wick to form within that EQ zone and reverse away from it.
- Checked timeframe alignment: the **1-hour was also opening a C3**, and the **30-minute was also opening a C3** — every relevant timeframe opening its continuation candle at the same moment.

## What that alignment means

When 4H, 1H, and 30M are all simultaneously in C3, that's the signal to expect **order-block-style continuation** (a change in delivery) on the lower timeframe rather than a fresh gap/swing setup — because the market already has an existing swing structure and doesn't need to build a new one first.

## The entry

Positioned within the candle's wick — formed right around the measured EQ level — using the lower-timeframe order flow, rather than waiting for a traditional gap-and-SMT setup that was never going to form in time.

## Takeaway

This is the practical version of [[Simultaneous C3 Across Timeframes (No Swing Forms)]]: recognize the multi-timeframe C3 alignment *before* the move happens, measure EQ as your reaction zone, and position immediately rather than waiting for a setup that isn't coming.

\# Example 4 — Gold, 2AM Reversal, Two-Stage PSP Strength Switch

← [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]] · Concept: [[Two-Stage SMT for the Reversal Candle]]

## 4H setup

A 02:00 reversal on Gold — but **zero SMT** on Gold itself at that point. Not tradable yet; wait for the next candle.

## Building the two stages

- Checked **Silver**: Silver takes out this low — but that's only **one stage** of confirmation on its own.
- Checked the **1-hour chart** for a second stage — none found there; instead it just leads into further expansion.
- Dropped to the **30-minute chart**, at the previous 4H low: SMT is present. On the 9:00 AM candle, one asset closes bearish while Gold closes bullish (or vice versa) — a **strength-switch PSP**. At the original SMT, Silver was the "weaker" asset; on this later candle, Silver flips to become the "stronger" one, while Gold flips from stronger to weaker.

## Why the flip matters

Because of this strength-switch PSP, the low is treated as **protected** even though Gold never printed a clean, full reversal-close candle at 02:00. The PSP substitutes for the missing textbook reversal.

## The trade

With the key level hit, SMT present, and the two-stage PSP confirmed, the plan shifts to trading Gold up toward a high. Positioned within the confirming candle, using down-closed candles supporting price to the upside as the trigger. Silver also reaches its own corresponding high.

## Takeaway

Demonstrates that a two-stage SMT doesn't have to be two separate, matching divergences — a **strength switch** (an asset flipping from weaker to stronger, or vice versa, between two candles) can itself serve as the second stage, especially when the reversal candle didn't close cleanly on its own.

## Related
- [[Two-Stage SMT for the Reversal Candle]]
- [[0200 Reversal]]

\# Example 5 — Gold, Driver (9:30) Continuation Inside C2

← [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]] · Concept: [[Drivers - The Time Exception]]

## 4H setup

Internal range liquidity is hit, with SMT at a low, and an external draw sits above. No two-stage SMT yet, so the plan is to let continuation happen **within the current candle (C2)** rather than trading the reversal directly.

## Lower-timeframe confirmation

Dropped to the **hourly chart**: price taps into a gap, and SMT confirms inside it — this candle's low holds on Gold but gets taken out on the correlated asset. That's the trigger to start positioning to the upside.

Dropped to the **30-minute chart**: the SMT is pinpointed there. **9:30 delivers price higher**, and **10:00 finishes the move**, reaching the draw on liquidity.

## Why this works despite limited time

Under the normal [[Time Remaining in C2 - The Core Decision Tree|timing rules]], not having "enough time to expand" in the candle would normally push this toward waiting for C3. Here, that's overridden because the **9:30 driver** is coming up — it's assumed to deliver price to the draw on liquidity regardless of how much raw time is left in the candle.

## Takeaway

This is the canonical example of [[Drivers - The Time Exception]]: the only circumstance under which continuation is traded inside a C2 candle that otherwise wouldn't have enough time to expand.

## Related
- [[Drivers - The Time Exception]]
- [[Trading Continuation Inside C2 (Enough Time Left)]]

\# Example 6 — Gold, C2 Continuation With Time Left

← [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]] · Concept: [[Trading Continuation Inside C2 (Enough Time Left)]]

## 4H setup

SMT confirmed at a low on Gold; the plan is to trade Gold up to a high. Dropped to the **1-hour chart**: a swing is visible, but there's no two-stage confirmation there.

## Finding the entry

Dropped to the **30-minute chart**: a gap is present that can be used to trade toward the highs. This is usable specifically because there's still **about an hour and a half left** in the candle — enough time for the setup to actually develop and reach the draw.

## Confirmation

SMT is present inside that gap: the **8:30 candle** closes bullish on one asset and bearish on the correlated one — a strength-switch, used as confirmation to trade toward the highs. Positioned at that candle's open.

## Takeaway

A clean example of [[Trading Continuation Inside C2 (Enough Time Left)]]: enough time remaining plus a small wick made a direct C2 entry viable, without needing to wait for C3 or rely on a driver.

\# Example 7 — Continuation, Equal Highs, 1H Swing Inside a Gap

← [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]] · Concept: [[The Wick-in-Gap Alignment Setup]]

## 4H setup

A key level is hit, forming a valid low of day (key level + reversal). Equal highs sit above as the draw on liquidity. SMT is present between two candles, and on Gold there's a full **two-stage** confirmation via a PSP.

## Why the entry wasn't taken immediately

Equal highs above meant conviction needed extra confirmation before committing fully — described as wanting to see continuation confirmed on the lower timeframe first, rather than jumping in purely off the two-stage SMT.

## Lower-timeframe alignment

06:00 opens into a gap. The requirement: a swing needs to form **inside that gap, with SMT**.

- On **Gold**: the 07:00 candle does **not** take out 06:00's low.
- On **Silver**: 06:00's low **is** taken out at 07:00.

That divergence between the two assets is the aligned 1-hour swing point.

## The result

Delivery follows at **08:00 AM** — a clean 4H continuation aligned with a 1-hour swing point inside a key level.

## Closing takeaway from the source material

This example is used to reinforce [[Why 30M and 1H, Not 15M]]: these continuation-aligned trades on the 30-minute/1-hour charts are described as the highest-probability setups in this framework, and dropping to the 15-minute chart is explicitly discouraged as a source of confusion and overtrading.

\# 4H Session Map

← [[4H Profiling]]

The trading day is read as six 4-hour candles (NY time). Each one has a name and a role in the framework.

| Time | Nickname | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 18:00 | Daily open | First candle after daily open — can set the tone for the whole day |
| 22:00 | 10pm | Overnight expansion candle |
| 02:00 | 2am | London-adjacent, first real NY-setup candle |
| 06:00 | 6am | Pre-NY, best NY-setup candle |
| 10:00 | 10am | NY primary session — reversal *into* expansion rather than "wait for next candle" |
| 14:00 | 2pm | Excluded — see [[1400 - No Trade]] |

## Why the order matters

Every candle after 18:00 inherits context from the ones before it. The core question you're asking on each candle is always the same:

1. Did this candle create a new high or low of day?
2. Did it close back against that wick (a reversal candle)?
3. Is there [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]] confirming it?

If yes to all three, see [[Reversal Profile Logic]] for what happens next. If the candle instead just extends an existing move with no new high/low, see [[Straight Expansion - No Trade]].

## Related
- [[Reversal Profile Logic]]
- [[Session Probability Map]]

\# Reversal Profile Logic

← [[4H Profiling]] · See also [[4H Session Map]]

## The core assumption

Whenever a 4H candle **reverses** — meaning it creates the high of day or low of day and then closes back against that wick — you assume the **next** 4H candle will continue in the direction of the reversal, not the direction of the original wick.

This chains forward one candle at a time:

- 18:00 reverses → expect **22:00** to continue
- 22:00 reverses → expect **02:00** to continue
- 02:00 reverses → expect **06:00** to continue
- 06:00 reverses → expect **10:00** to continue
- 10:00 is treated differently — it reverses *and* expands within its own candle, see [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]]
- 14:00 is excluded, see [[1400 - No Trade]]

## This is a mental model, not a trade signal by itself

A reversal candle is only a *thesis*. It does not become tradable until it clears the [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT confirmation]] gate. Two outcomes:

- **SMT present on the reversal candle** → the reversal itself is tradable.
- **No SMT on the reversal candle** → don't trade that candle. Instead wait for the *next* candle to open and confirm the reversal (e.g. it engulfs the prior price action and closes beyond the bodies), then treat that as the entry — see [[Continuation Entry - Gap Method]] and [[Continuation Entry - Swing SMT Method]] for how this is actually executed on lower timeframes.

## Why probability isn't uniform across candles

Not every reversal carries the same odds into New York. An 18:00 or 22:00 reversal has a lot of "runway" left before NY opens, so the daily range may already be substantially used by the time NY arrives — this caps how far NY can realistically continue. A 02:00 or 06:00 reversal happens much closer to NY, so there's more range left to expand into. Full breakdown: [[Session Probability Map]].

- [[Session Probability Map]]
- [[Wick Size Rule]]

\# Session Probability Map

← [[4H Profiling]] · See also [[Reversal Profile Logic]]

## The core idea

The daily candle can only expand so far. Every hour of expansion that happens *before* New York opens eats into the range that would otherwise be available for NY to use. That means **which candle produces the reversal changes how probable New York is**, independent of the setup quality itself.

## Early reversals (18:00 / 22:00) → New York is low probability

If 18:00 or 22:00 creates the high or low of day and expansion runs from there, by the time NY opens most of the "easy" range has already been used. Two outcomes to plan for:

1. **Straight continuous expansion into NY** → NY is unlikely to just keep extending in the same direction. Treat NY as a session to either **avoid**, or trade **only as a retracement** back toward the origin. A new 4H high/low would be required to justify fresh continuation, and that's a new setup, not this one.
2. **A consolidation forms first** (e.g. London consolidates after the 18:00/22:00 expansion) → this resets the clock. A brand-new 4H profile can form out of that consolidation, and NY continuation becomes viable again — but it's being traded as its own new profile, not as a direct extension of the 18:00/22:00 move.

## Late reversals (02:00 / 06:00) → New York is high probability

02:00 and 06:00 sit much closer to the NY session. When one of these reverses, there's still plenty of daily range left, and the very next candle in the chain (06:00 or 10:00) lands inside or right at the start of NY. This is why the source material treats 02:00 and 06:00 reversals as the **best** New York setups — the reversal and the payoff session are close together.

## 10:00 is its own category

10:00 doesn't follow "reversal now, continuation next candle" — it reverses *and* expands within the same candle. Probability here isn't about which candle comes next, it's about wick size. See [[Wick Size Rule]] and [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]].

\# SMT Confirmation Rule

← [[4H Profiling]] · See also [[Reversal Profile Logic]]

## The rule

**You need SMT to trade any reversal candle.** This applies to every session — 18:00, 22:00, 02:00, 06:00, and 10:00. Without it, the reversal candle itself is not tradable.

SMT (Smart Money Technique) here means: a correlated asset **fails to confirm** the same high or low. Example pairs used throughout the framework:

- Gold vs. Silver
- NQ vs. YM (or ES)
- Euro vs. GBP (for indirect/PSP-style confirmation — see [[Two-Stage SMT (PSP Confirmation)]])

If your asset takes out a high/low and closes as a reversal candle, but the correlated asset does **not** take out the equivalent high/low, that divergence is the SMT — and it's what makes the reversal candle tradable.

## Where to look for it

- Primarily on the 4H chart itself, on the reversal candle.
- If the 4H doesn't show a clean SMT, drop down to the **1H chart** and look for it there instead. This is explicitly allowed — SMT doesn't have to appear on the same timeframe as the reversal candle.

## If there's no SMT

Don't force the reversal candle. Instead:

1. Wait for the next 4H candle to print.
2. If that next candle **engulfs** the prior price action and closes beyond the bodies of the reversal candle's range, treat that as confirmation the reversal is real.
3. Trade the continuation from there — see [[Continuation Entry - Gap Method]] and [[Continuation Entry - Swing SMT Method]] for the lower-timeframe execution.

## Related
- [[Reversal Profile Logic]]
- [[Two-Stage SMT (PSP Confirmation)]]
- [[NASDAQ - 2200 Reversal (Wait for Confirmation) Example]] — worked example of "no SMT, wait for next candle"

\# Straight Expansion - No Trade

← [[4H Profiling]] · See also [[Session Probability Map]]

## The rule

If the daily candle just expands continuously in one direction with **no significant high or low created** — no reversal candle, no clear structural high/low of day — **avoid the session.**

Example: 18:00 opens and price just keeps expanding in one direction straight through to when New York opens. There's no reversal, no consolidation, nothing to react to. In that case, don't trade New York.

## Why

The daily candle can only expand so far in one direction. Without a retracement or a fresh high/low forming somewhere in the sequence, there's no reasonable basis to expect NY to just keep extending the same move. Continuously expecting a trend to keep expanding for no structural reason isn't a setup — it's a guess.

## The exception

If a **new 4H high or low is created** (rather than just a straight, structureless push), that's a different situation — that new high/low can be reacted to like any other reversal profile. And if the market **consolidates** before the next session instead of expanding straight through, a new 4H profile can form out of that consolidation, which is tradable (see [[Session Probability Map]] for how this plays out with 18:00/22:00 reversals specifically).

## Related
- [[Session Probability Map]]
- [[Reversal Profile Logic]]

\# Two-Stage SMT (PSP Confirmation)

← [[4H Profiling]] · See also [[SMT Confirmation Rule]]

## What it is

A second layer of confirmation used on top of the basic [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT rule]], specifically useful on Gold. Instead of (or in addition to) checking whether a correlated metal takes out the same high/low, you check whether **correlated currency pairs close their candle in the same direction as your bias**, forming a PSP (price/candle-close divergence) across the basket.

Example basket used: **Euro, GBP, Gold**.

## How it's applied

On a 2:00 candle, for instance:

1. Check if Gold takes out the prior high and closes bearish.
2. Check Silver — does it fail to take out the same high (basic SMT)?
3. Check Euro and GBP — do they also close their 2:00 candle **bearish**, while Gold's own candle read would otherwise be ambiguous or contradicted?

If Euro closes bearish, GBP closes bearish, and Gold's read lines up with them (even if Gold's own candle isn't a clean textbook reversal), that basket-level agreement is the "two-stage" confirmation — it makes the downside bias on Gold favorable.

## Important caution from the source material

Don't assume a two-stage setup exists just because one leg looks right — verify on the actual traded contract, not just a cleaner-looking alternate contract. In the source example, switching from an alternate gold contract to the regular contract changed the read: what looked like a two-stage PSP on the alternate contract wasn't actually there on the regular contract. The conclusion (bearish bias, tradable via standard SMT) still held, but the extra "two-stage" label didn't apply — always confirm on the instrument you intend to trade.

## Related
- [[SMT Confirmation Rule]]
- [[Gold - 0200 Reversal (Two-Stage SMT) Example]]

\# Wick Size Rule

← [[4H Profiling]] · Primarily used in [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]]

## The rule

When a reversal candle's wick is **small** relative to the distance to the draw on liquidity, expansion can continue all the way to that draw. When the wick is **large** — meaning price already traveled most of the way to the draw just to form the wick — don't expect the same follow-through. A large wick has already "spent" most of the available range.

## How to apply it

- **Small wick + obvious draw on liquidity (equal highs/lows, untouched level)** → prefer this setup, expect the expansion to reach the draw.
- **Large wick** → you can still trade it, but lower your target. Expect it to reach nearby session highs/lows rather than the full draw on liquidity. Don't assume a large wick will still produce a large expansion — most of the move already happened inside the wick itself.

## Why this matters most on the 10:00 candle

This shows up most clearly on [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]] because that candle both reverses *and* expands within itself — there's no "wait for the next candle" buffer. The wick you get on the reversal *is* the move so far, so its size directly tells you how much is left.

## Worked examples
- [[NQ - 1000 Reversal Expansion Example (Small Wick)]] — small wick, full expansion to equal highs/lows
- [[NQ - 1000 Reversal Expansion Example (Range Trade)]] — larger wick, treated as an internal range trade to nearby equal lows instead of the full external draw

## Related
- [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]]
- [[Session Probability Map]]

\# 02:00 Reversal (2am)

← [[4H Profiling]] · Previous: [[2200 Reversal]] · Next: [[0600 Reversal]]

## Setup

The 02:00 candle creates the high of day or low of day and closes back against that wick.

## Requirements to trade it

Needs [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]]. This is also a good place to check [[Two-Stage SMT (PSP Confirmation)]] — correlated-currency PSP agreement — for extra conviction, especially on Gold.

## What to expect next

Assume **06:00 and 10:00** continue the reversal toward the draw on liquidity — see [[Reversal Profile Logic]].

## New York implications

This is where New York starts becoming genuinely high-probable. Per [[Session Probability Map]], 02:00 is close enough to the NY session that there's still real range left to work with — a much better risk/reward setup than an 18:00 or 22:00 origin.

## Extra technique: 50% measurement

You can measure the 50% level of the previous candle's range and look for the reversal wick to form around that 50% area — an added layer of confluence on top of the SMT requirement.

## Worked examples
- [[Gold - 0200 Reversal (Two-Stage SMT) Example]] — new week opening gap as target, two-stage SMT across Gold/Silver/Euro/GBP
- [[NASDAQ - 0200 Reversal Example]] — SMT vs YM, 50% measurement confluence, 06:00/10:00 continue to a gap

- [[Two-Stage SMT (PSP Confirmation)]]

\# 06:00 Reversal (6am)

← [[4H Profiling]] · Previous: [[0200 Reversal]] · Next: [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]]

## Setup

The 06:00 candle takes out session highs or lows, creates the high or low of day, and reverses away from it, closing as a reversal candle.

- Bearish version: 06:00 takes out session highs, creates high of day, reverses down.
- Bullish version: 06:00 takes out session lows, creates low of day, reverses up.

## Requirements to trade it

Needs [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]], same as every other profile candle.

## What to expect next

Assume **10:00** continues the 06:00 reversal — see [[Reversal Profile Logic]].

## New York implications

This is the **best** New York setup in the framework. Per [[Session Probability Map]], 06:00 sits right before NY, so a 06:00 reversal with 10:00 continuation is about as close as this model gets to a direct, high-probability NY play.

\# 10:00 Reversal into Expansion (10am)

← [[4H Profiling]] · Previous: [[0600 Reversal]] · Next: [[1400 - No Trade]]

## Setup

This profile is structurally different from the others: instead of reversing and waiting for the *next* candle to continue, the 10:00 candle creates the high or low of day and **expands within its own candle / the moves immediately following it.**

## Requirements to trade it

Needs [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]]. If the 4H doesn't show a clean SMT, drop to the **1H chart** and look for it there — this is explicitly allowed.

## The wick size decision

This is the single most important variable on this profile. See [[Wick Size Rule]] in full, but in short:

- **Small wick** relative to the draw on liquidity → prefer this, expect the expansion to actually reach the draw.
- **Large wick** → still tradable, but expect a smaller move. Target nearby session highs/lows rather than the full draw — most of the range was already used forming the wick.

## Execution

After the reversal + SMT confirms, drop down to the 1H → 30M → 15M charts to find the actual **swing formation with SMT** for entry. This is where the lower-timeframe execution layer of the framework kicks in — see [[HTF to LTF Transition Mindset]] and [[Continuation Entry - Swing SMT Method]].

## Why indices > metals for this profile

Metals (gold, silver) tend to move heavily in the overnight session, so by 10:00 the high/low of day is often already set elsewhere. Indices are less likely to have already made their day's high/low overnight, which makes the 10:00 candle a more reliable high/low-of-day maker on indices.

## Worked examples
- [[NQ - 1000 Reversal Expansion Example (Small Wick)]] — small wick, equal highs as draw, full expansion + LTF swing entry
- [[NQ - 1000 Reversal Expansion Example (Range Trade)]] — larger wick, nearby equal lows used instead of the full external draw (internal range trade)

## Related
- [[Wick Size Rule]]
- [[SMT Confirmation Rule]]
- [[HTF to LTF Transition Mindset]]

\# 14:00 — No Trade (2pm)

← [[4H Profiling]] · Previous: [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]] · Next: —

## The rule

The 14:00 candle is **not traded** in this framework. It is excluded from the reversal chain entirely — there is no "14:00 reversal profile."

## Why

2pm is a slow, lethargic session. It doesn't produce reliable reversal or continuation behavior the way 18:00, 22:00, 02:00, 06:00, and 10:00 do, so building a profile around it isn't worthwhile.

## Practical note

If the draw on liquidity from an earlier reversal (e.g. a [[2200 Reversal]]) hasn't been met yet, 14:00 can still passively continue toward it — but that's inherited momentum from an earlier setup, not a 14:00 profile in its own right.

\# 18:00 Reversal — Daily Open Reversal

← [[4H Profiling]] · Previous: — · Next: [[2200 Reversal]]

## Setup

The 18:00 candle (daily open) creates the high of day or low of day and closes back against that wick — a reversal candle.

## Requirements to trade it

Needs [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]] — a correlated asset failing to take out the equivalent high/low. Without SMT, this candle is not tradable; wait for confirmation on the next candle instead (see [[SMT Confirmation Rule]]).

## What to expect next

Assume **22:00** continues the reversal — see [[Reversal Profile Logic]].

## New York implications

Because this is the earliest candle in the daily cycle, by the time New York opens a large portion of the day's range may already be used. Per [[Session Probability Map]]:

- If expansion runs straight through into NY with no consolidation, **treat NY as low probability** — either avoid it or only trade it as a **retracement** back toward the 18:00 origin.
- If **London consolidates** before NY, that consolidation can produce a *new* 4H profile, making a fresh NY continuation trade viable — but as its own setup, not a direct extension of 18:00.

## Worked examples
- [[Gold - 1800 Reversal Example]] — SMT vs Silver, 22:00 continuation, then a 2am/6am retracement into NY
- [[NQ - 1800 Reversal Example]] — SMT vs YM, consolidation before NY enables a NY continuation

\# 22:00 Reversal (10pm)

← [[4H Profiling]] · Previous: [[1800 Reversal - Daily Open]] · Next: [[0200 Reversal]]

## Setup

The 22:00 candle creates the high of day or low of day and closes back against that wick.

## Requirements to trade it

Needs [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]]. If there's no reversal candle and no SMT at 22:00, **don't trade it** — wait for 02:00 to print and confirm (engulfing the prior range, closing beyond the bodies), then trade the continuation from there.

## What to expect next

Assume **02:00, 06:00, and 10:00** all continue the expansion in the direction of the reversal (internal liquidity → external liquidity, chaining forward through the remaining candles) — see [[Reversal Profile Logic]].

## New York implications

Same logic as [[1800 Reversal - Daily Open]] applies: this is still an early-cycle reversal, so per [[Session Probability Map]] New York's continuation probability is lower than a 02:00 or 06:00 origin. Watch for whether the draw on liquidity has actually been met before assuming further continuation into the 14:00 candle.

## Worked examples
- [[Indices - 2200 Reversal Example]] — SMT vs Silver overnight high, deep retracement holds, 02:00/06:00/10:00 all continue
- [[NASDAQ - 2200 Reversal (Wait for Confirmation) Example]] — no reversal candle, no SMT at 22:00; 02:00 confirms instead

\# Continuation Entry — Gap Method

← [[4H Profiling]] · See also [[HTF to LTF Transition Mindset]]

## When to use this

You missed the 4H reversal candle itself, but the framework says the *next* 4H candle should continue the move (per [[Reversal Profile Logic]]). Instead of chasing price on the 4H, drop down to find an entry inside the corresponding lower-timeframe candle (1H, 30M, or 15M).

## The method

1. Zoom into the lower-timeframe candle that lines up with the 4H continuation candle.
2. Look for a **gap** (a fair value gap / imbalance) forming within that candle's price action.
3. Wait for a **new candle to open, tap back into that gap**, and then expand away from it — ideally with the gap-fill also forming the body of that new candle.
4. That tap-and-expand is the entry, using the gap as your confirmation that the continuation is real.

## Why this works

Gaps left behind during an impulsive continuation move tend to get revisited briefly before the move resumes. Waiting for price to return into the gap and then push away gives you a defined, lower-risk entry instead of entering into the middle of an already-extended move.

## If there's no gap

Don't force this method. Use [[Continuation Entry - Swing SMT Method]] instead.

## Related
- [[HTF to LTF Transition Mindset]]
- [[Continuation Entry - Swing SMT Method]]
- [[Reversal Profile Logic]]

\# Continuation Entry — Swing SMT Method

← [[4H Profiling]] · See also [[HTF to LTF Transition Mindset]]

## When to use this

You're looking for a lower-timeframe entry into a confirmed 4H continuation, but there's **no gap** to use for [[Continuation Entry - Gap Method|the gap method]].

## The method

Instead of a gap, look for a **swing formation with SMT** on the lower timeframe (1H, 30M, or 15M) — the exact same logic as [[SMT Confirmation Rule]], just applied one or two timeframes down:

1. Identify a swing high or low forming on the LTF in the direction the 4H context says price should go.
2. Check a correlated asset for divergence at that same swing point (the correlated asset fails to make the equivalent high/low).
3. That divergence is your SMT, and the swing point it confirms is your entry structure.

## Why this is the fallback

Gaps are a fast, visual confirmation but don't always form. A swing + SMT is the same core confirmation tool used throughout the entire 4H framework ([[SMT Confirmation Rule]]) — it's reliable at any timeframe, which is why it's the default fallback whenever the faster gap read isn't available.

## Related
- [[HTF to LTF Transition Mindset]]
- [[Continuation Entry - Gap Method]]
- [[SMT Confirmation Rule]]
- [[NQ - 1000 Reversal Expansion Example (Small Wick)]] — shows this method applied on the 30M/15M charts

\# HTF to LTF Transition Mindset

← [[4H Profiling]]

## The mental shift

Everything in [[1 Core Framework]] and [[2 Session Profiles]] happens on the 4H chart and answers one question: *what should happen next, and is it confirmed?* Once that question is answered — a candle has reversed, SMT is present or the next candle has confirmed it — the job shifts from **reading** to **executing**. That execution happens on the 1H, 30M, or 15M chart.

Don't skip this step. A confirmed 4H thesis is not itself an entry — it's a context. The entry is found on the lower timeframe.

## Two execution paths

Which path you use depends on whether you caught the reversal candle itself:

1. **You missed the reversal candle** → look for a gap inside the corresponding lower-timeframe candle and enter on the retest. See [[Continuation Entry - Gap Method]].
2. **No gap is present** → look for a swing formation with its own SMT on the lower timeframe instead. See [[Continuation Entry - Swing SMT Method]].

SMT itself is scale-independent — if the 4H doesn't show it, the 1H might. The same is true going the other direction: if you missed the 4H-level entry, the 1H can generate its own valid swing + SMT setup.

## Scope note

This note only covers the *mindset* — recognizing that a transition needs to happen and picking the right method. The full mechanics of aligning a specific 1H or 30M swing to a 4H profile — including the C1/C2/C3 candle framework, two-stage SMT, and, importantly, how much time is left in the current 4H candle changes whether you trade the continuation now or wait for the next candle — is covered in depth in its own hub: [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]].

\# Example: Gold — 02:00 Reversal with Two-Stage SMT

← [[4H Profiling]] · Profile: [[0200 Reversal]] · Technique: [[Two-Stage SMT (PSP Confirmation)]]

## Setup

New week opens with a **new week opening gap** left unfilled — this becomes the primary draw on liquidity / target for the session. The 02:00 candle puts in a reversal.

## Confirmation

- On Silver: the prior high does **not** get taken out while Gold's candle prints bearish — basic [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]].
- Checked correlated currencies for [[Two-Stage SMT (PSP Confirmation)|two-stage confirmation]]: Euro closes bearish, GBP closes bearish, agreeing with the bearish Gold read — favoring gold to the downside.

## Important correction from the source material

When switching from an alternate gold contract to the **regular gold contract**, the two-stage PSP wasn't actually present — it only looked that way on the alternate contract. The underlying conclusion held (basic SMT confirmed the reversal candle as tradable), but the "two-stage" label didn't apply on the instrument actually being traded. Always verify on the contract you intend to trade.

## What happened

02:00 reverses with confirmed SMT → **06:00 and 10:00 continue** to the draw on liquidity (the new week opening gap).

## Takeaway

Illustrates both the [[0200 Reversal]] profile and the discipline point in [[Two-Stage SMT (PSP Confirmation)]]: don't assume a confluence factor exists just because a related chart suggests it — confirm on the actual traded instrument.

\# Example: Gold — 18:00 Reversal

← [[4H Profiling]] · Profile: [[1800 Reversal - Daily Open]]

## Setup

18:00 opens and takes out the previous day's high.

## Confirmation

Checked Silver for [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]] — Silver prints the divergence, confirming the reversal candle is tradable.

## What happened

- **22:00 continues** the reversal into expansion, exactly as the profile predicts.
- Later, a **02:00 reversal** forms, followed by a **06:00 retracement** during New York.
- New York plays out as a retracement back into the range rather than fresh continuation — consistent with [[Session Probability Map]]'s point that an 18:00-origin reversal makes NY lower probability once the move has already expanded.

## Takeaway

Textbook case of: 18:00 reverses (with SMT) → 22:00 continues → NY retraces rather than extends.

\# Example: Indices — 22:00 Reversal (High of Day)

← [[4H Profiling]] · Profile: [[2200 Reversal]]

## Setup

22:00 (10pm) puts in the high of day, hitting internal range liquidity, and closes as a reversal candle (internal-to-external liquidity read).

## Confirmation

Checked Silver — the 18:00 high **stays intact** (22:00 does not create a new high there), which is the [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]] confirming this reversal candle is tradable.

## What happened

- Price comes back up and nearly retests the 22:00 high, but it holds as a **protected high** because of the SMT — a deep retracement, not a break.
- From there: **02:00 continues**, then **06:00 continues**, then **10:00 continues**.
- Since the draw on liquidity still hadn't been fully met, even **14:00 continues** toward the remaining target.

## Takeaway

This is the full reversal chain from [[Reversal Profile Logic]] playing out candle by candle: 22:00 reverses (with SMT) → 02:00 → 06:00 → 10:00 (→ 14:00) all continue toward the same draw on liquidity.

\# Example: NASDAQ — 02:00 Reversal

← [[4H Profiling]] · Profile: [[0200 Reversal]]

## Setup

Leaves a series of failure swings below price, targeting a gap above as the draw on liquidity. 02:00 prints a reversal candle (closes bullish on this instance).

## Confirmation

- No SMT on ES.
- SMT found on **YM**: a prior day's low (from the prior Tuesday) is taken out on NQ but stays intact on YM — that's the [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]] making this tradable to the downside/reversal direction.
- No two-stage PSP present on this one — checked and ruled out (contrast with [[Gold - 0200 Reversal (Two-Stage SMT) Example]]).

## Extra confluence

The reversal wick formed close to the **50% level** of the previous candle's range — the measurement technique noted in [[0200 Reversal]].

## What happened

02:00 reverses with SMT confirmed → **06:00 and 10:00 continue** toward the gap target.

## Takeaway

A clean, single-stage SMT confirmation (not every setup needs the two-stage PSP layer) combined with the 50% measurement as extra confluence.

\# Example: NASDAQ — 22:00 High With No Confirmation (Wait for 02:00)

← [[4H Profiling]] · Profile: [[2200 Reversal]]

## Setup

22:00 creates the high of day on NASDAQ, but it does **not** close as a reversal candle.

## Confirmation check — fails

- No SMT on ES.
- No SMT on YM.
- The prior session high remains intact across correlated assets, but with no reversal candle *and* no SMT, this is **not tradable** per [[SMT Confirmation Rule]].

## What to do instead

Don't force the 22:00 candle. Wait for **02:00** to print. When the 02:00 candle **engulfs** the prior price action and closes below the bodies of those candles, that's the confirmation that the 22:00 high was in fact a reversal.

## What happened

- 02:00 confirms the reversal by engulfing and closing below the relevant candle bodies.
- From there, **06:00 and 10:00** are expected to continue the (now-confirmed) 22:00 reversal.

## Takeaway

This is the practical version of the "no SMT → wait for the next candle" rule from [[SMT Confirmation Rule]]. A high/low of day forming without a clean reversal candle or SMT isn't a dead setup — it's a setup that needs one more candle of confirmation before it's tradable.

\# Example: NQ — 10:00 Reversal into Expansion (Range Trade)

← [[4H Profiling]] · Profile: [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]] · Rule: [[Wick Size Rule]]

## Setup

A key level (a high) is in play with SMT confirming it between correlated assets. Indices are favored for this profile since metals often already set their day's high/low overnight (see [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]]).

## Confirmation

SMT present between the correlated assets at the key high.

## Wick size note

The wick here is **relatively large** — normally a caution flag per [[Wick Size Rule]]. But nearby **equal lows** provide a legitimate, *closer* draw on liquidity, so the large wick doesn't need to reach a distant external target — it only needs to reach the nearby internal one.

## What happened

Effectively an **internal range trade**: take the internal high (with SMT), return to the internal low (the equal lows). Confirmed by dropping to the **1-hour chart**, where an hourly swing forms, giving continuation entries on lower timeframes from there.

## Takeaway

Contrast with [[NQ - 1000 Reversal Expansion Example (Small Wick)]]: same profile, but because the wick was large, the draw was rescoped to the nearest available liquidity (equal lows) instead of a distant external target. This is the large-wick branch of [[Wick Size Rule]] in practice.

\# Example: NQ — 10:00 Reversal into Expansion (Small Wick)

← [[4H Profiling]] · Profile: [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]] · Rule: [[Wick Size Rule]]

## Setup

Equal highs sit above price, left untouched — an obvious draw on liquidity. Price first prints an SMT on the way up, then reverses.

## Confirmation

Found SMT vs **YM** confirming the setup is not tradable at the very first touch (the initial candle closure doesn't qualify) — so the plan becomes: expect **10:00 to take out the 06:00 low** instead of reacting immediately.

Dropped to the **30-minute chart**: a 30-minute reversal candle prints, with the same equal-highs SMT visible there. This confirms the 10:00 candle closing bullish/bearish opposite pairing between the two correlated assets — the SMT.

## What happened

- NQ takes out the 06:00 low (weaker candle close signaled this was likely rather than an SMT-only reaction).
- SMT confirmed with a PSP at that low.
- Expansion follows.
- Dropped to the **15-minute chart** to find the actual swing point for entry — a clean swing forms there (and correspondingly on YM), per [[Continuation Entry - Swing SMT Method]].

## Wick size note

This is a **small wick** relative to the draw (the equal highs) — per [[Wick Size Rule]], that's what allows the full expansion to actually reach the draw, rather than stalling early.

## Takeaway

Full pipeline in one example: 4H reversal + SMT → HTF context set → drop to 30M for confirmation → drop to 15M for the swing entry.

\# Example: NQ — 18:00 Reversal

← [[4H Profiling]] · Profile: [[1800 Reversal - Daily Open]]

## Setup

18:00 creates the **low of day** on NQ.

## Confirmation

The low taken out on NQ stays **intact on YM** — that divergence is the [[SMT Confirmation Rule|SMT]] confirming the reversal is tradable.

## What happened

- The candles immediately following the reversal **consolidate** rather than continuing straight away.
- Because that consolidation happens *before* New York, per [[Session Probability Map]] it effectively resets the setup — a new profile forms out of the consolidation.
- New York then trades as a **continuation** of the original 18:00 reversal (reversal → expansion → consolidation → expansion again).

## Takeaway

Contrast with [[Gold - 1800 Reversal Example]]: same 18:00-origin reversal, but because price consolidated instead of running straight through into NY, NY became a viable continuation trade instead of a retracement-only session. This is the practical version of the "London consolidates" exception in [[Session Probability Map]].

\# 4H Profiling

Central hub for the 4-hour profile framework. This is a top-down model: each 4H candle in the daily cycle either **reverses** (creates the high/low of day and closes back against it) or **continues** an existing move. Reading which one just happened tells you what to expect from the *next* 4H candle — and how probable the New York session is going to be.

This vault section covers the HTF mental framework only. Aligning a specific 1H/30M swing to a 4H profile is a separate skill covered in another video (linked in [[HTF to LTF Transition Mindset]]).

> For a deeper, more complete treatment of this entire subject — including the C2/C3 closure filter, valid vs. invalid reversal signatures, fractal alignment across daily/4H/1H, and one-stage vs. two-stage SMT — see [[Candle Profiling - Complete Framework]].

---

## 1. Core Framework
The rules that apply across every profile, regardless of which candle you're on.

- [[4H Session Map]] — the six 4H candles and how they divide the day
- [[Reversal Profile Logic]] — the core reversal → continuation assumption
- [[SMT Confirmation Rule]] — the gate that makes a reversal candle tradable
- [[Two-Stage SMT (PSP Confirmation)]] — using correlated-asset PSPs to pick a side
- [[Session Probability Map]] — why early reversals (1800/2200) make NY low-probability and late reversals (0200/0600) make NY high-probability
- [[Wick Size Rule]] — reading wick size to judge how far a reversal can expand
- [[Straight Expansion - No Trade]] — when to just avoid the session entirely

## 2. Session Profiles
Each 4H candle, one at a time.

- [[1800 Reversal - Daily Open]]
- [[2200 Reversal]]
- [[0200 Reversal]]
- [[0600 Reversal]]
- [[1000 Reversal - Expansion]]
- [[1400 - No Trade]]

## 3. Lower Timeframe Execution
Once the 4H context is set, how you actually get an entry.

- [[HTF to LTF Transition Mindset]]
- [[Continuation Entry - Gap Method]]
- [[Continuation Entry - Swing SMT Method]]

## 4. Chart Examples
Worked examples pulled straight from the source video, organized by profile.

- [[Gold - 1800 Reversal Example]]
- [[NQ - 1800 Reversal Example]]
- [[Indices - 2200 Reversal Example]]
- [[NASDAQ - 2200 Reversal (Wait for Confirmation) Example]]
- [[Gold - 0200 Reversal (Two-Stage SMT) Example]]
- [[NASDAQ - 0200 Reversal Example]]
- [[NQ - 1000 Reversal Expansion Example (Small Wick)]]
- [[NQ - 1000 Reversal Expansion Example (Range Trade)]]

---

## The One-Sentence Version

> A 4H candle that reverses and creates the high/low of day is a signal, not a trade — it only becomes tradable with SMT confirmation, and it tells you which direction the *next* candle should continue toward liquidity.

## Quick Reference Table

| Candle (NY time) | If it reverses, expect continuation from... | NY probability if this is the origin |
|---|---|---|
| 18:00 (6pm) | 22:00 | Low — NY likely retraces unless London consolidates first |
| 22:00 (10pm) | 02:00 → 06:00 → 10:00 | Low-medium — same logic, range may already be used up |
| 02:00 (2am) | 06:00 → 10:00 | High — good NY continuation setup |
| 06:00 (6am) | 10:00 | High — best NY continuation setup |
| 10:00 (10am) | Expansion within its own candle | Depends on wick size, see [[Wick Size Rule]] |
| 14:00 (2pm) | — | Not traded — session too slow/lethargic |

\# Trading Requirements for C1

← [[Combining them]] · See also [[What Creates a C1]]

## The requirement: there isn't one, because C1 isn't a trade

C1 is a reference point, not a signal. There is no SMT check, no wick-size check, no gap check for C1 itself — because you are never entering **on** C1. Trying to trade a reversal directly off of C1, before its level has actually been engaged by a later candle, is trading away from a level that hasn't been tested yet. That's the mistake to avoid here: don't anticipate a reversal at a level before price has actually come back to interact with it.

## What "trading requirements" actually means for C1

The only thing that matters at the C1 stage is **correct identification**:

1. Confirm the level C1 leaves behind has real separation from neighboring swings (see [[What Creates a C1]]) — otherwise you're anchoring your whole C2/C3 expectation to a low-quality reference.
2. Once identified, do nothing except wait. The actual decision points come later, when a candle sweeps this level ([[What Creates a C2]]) and reverses.

## Why this matters

Misidentifying C1 — treating a failure swing as if it were a legitimate reference level — is the single most common way to build a false C2 expectation. If the "reversal" you're watching for never had a real level behind it, there was never a valid setup to begin with, regardless of how clean the candle that follows looks.

\# What C1 Looks Like on the Chart

← [[Combining them]] · See also [[What Creates a C1]]

## Visual signature

C1 has **no distinctive candle shape of its own** — that's what separates it from C2 and C3, both of which have specific wick/gap requirements. C1 is identified by what it *leaves behind*, not by how it closes.

Concretely, on the chart you're looking for:

- A clear swing low or swing high with price trading away from it afterward (an ordinary expansion or continuation candle, or a small cluster of candles that mark the extreme).
- **Distance/separation** from neighboring swing points. A cluster of closely-stacked highs (or lows) sitting near each other reads as failure swings, not a single clean C1 reference — see [[What Creates a C1]].
- Nothing about SMT or wick size is required here — those requirements only kick in once C2 reacts to this level.

## How to spot it in real time

Ask: "if price came back down (or up) to this level right now, would that actually mean something, or is this just noise close to other recent swings?" If it would mean something — if it's genuinely far enough away that reacting to it is a real event — you're looking at a valid C1. If it's one of several closely bunched highs/lows, you're looking at something closer to a failure swing, and price is far more likely to just run through it than react to it.

## Related
- [[What Creates a C1]]
- [[Trading Requirements for C1]]

\# What Creates a C1

← [[Combining them]]

## What it actually is

C1 isn't produced by a special mechanism of its own — it's simply **whichever candle establishes the low (or high) that C2 later sweeps and reverses away from.** There is no separate "C1 setup." Any candle that leaves behind a swing extreme can end up playing the role of C1 for the reversal that follows it.

## Where C1 comes from in practice

Most often, C1 is one of two things:

1. **An ordinary candle in the 4H chain** ([[4H Session Map]]) — e.g. if 06:00 is about to be the C2 reversal, then 02:00 (or whichever candle immediately precedes it and holds the relevant low) is C1.
2. **A previous cycle's C3** — because [[Reversal Profile Logic]] chains forward candle by candle, today's continuation candle is tomorrow's reference candle. See [[The Fractal Chain (C3 Becomes the Next C1)]] for the full mechanic.

## The one condition that matters: it has to be a *relevant* level

Not every prior low or high qualifies as a usable C1. If the level is too close to other recent swing points — a **failure swing** rather than a level with real separation — then sweeping it doesn't carry the same weight, and a "reversal" off of it is much lower quality. A valid C1 is a level with genuine distance from the swings around it, so that reacting to it actually means something.

This is the same distinction that governs [[Trading Requirements for C1]]: the reason C1 itself isn't a trade is bound up with whether it's even the right level to be paying attention to in the first place.

## Related

- [[Trading Requirements for C1]]

\# Trading Requirements for C2

← [[Combining them]] · See also [[What Creates a C2]]

There are two different things you might be trying to do with C2, and they have different requirements.

## Requirement set 1: treating C2 as confirmation (not entering yet)

At minimum, before C2 counts as a real reversal at all:

1. C1's level must be a **valid, relevant level** — see [[Trading Requirements for C1]].
2. **SMT** must confirm the sweep — a correlated asset fails to make the equivalent move. See [[SMT Confirmation Rule]].

If both hold, C2 is a confirmed reversal — you now expect C3 to continue (see [[What Creates a C3]]), even if you don't trade C2 itself.

## Requirement set 2: actually entering on C2

To position **inside C2** rather than waiting for C3, you additionally need:

3. **Two-stage SMT** — not just the first-stage divergence at the level, but a second, independent confirmation on the 1H/30M (a PSP, or a strength-switch between correlated assets). See [[Two-Stage SMT for the Reversal Candle]]. A single stage is explicitly *not enough* to trade C2.
4. **A small wick** — if the wick is large, don't expect this candle to also expand; wait for C3 instead. See [[Wick Size Rule]].
5. **Enough time left in the candle** — trading C2 directly is only done when there's meaningfully more than an hour left in it (roughly), or when a scheduled driver is coming up regardless of the clock. See [[Time Remaining in C2 - The Core Decision Tree]] and [[Drivers - The Time Exception]].

## If requirement set 2 isn't met

Don't force it. This is the single most common outcome: C2 confirms as a reversal (set 1 satisfied), but the two-stage SMT, wick size, or time-remaining conditions for actually entering aren't there. In that case, the correct move is to **wait for C3** — see [[What C3 Looks Like on the Chart]] and [[Missed C2 - Getting Onside at C3]].

## Related
- [[Two-Stage SMT for the Reversal Candle]]
- [[Time Remaining in C2 - The Core Decision Tree]]
- [[Missed C2 - Getting Onside at C3]]

\# What C2 Looks Like on the Chart

← [[Combining them]] · See also [[What Creates a C2]]

## Visual signature

- A wick that extends **beyond C1's low or high**.
- A **close back inside the prior range** — the body doesn't hold outside C1's level, it reclaims it. This is the "closed back inside the range" language used throughout [[4H Profiling]] and [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]].
- The wick's **size relative to the draw on liquidity** is diagnostic, not decorative:
  - **Small wick** → visually, the rejection looks tight relative to where the level was — most of the range is still ahead of price. This is the version that can also expand on its own (see [[Trading Requirements for C2]]).
  - **Large wick** → visually, the wick travels a long distance to reach the level before rejecting — most of the move already happened just to form the wick. Don't expect this version to expand further by itself.

## Where SMT shows up visually

Look at a correlated asset's candle over the same window: if your asset's wick pokes beyond the reference level but the correlated asset's candle **does not** make the equivalent move, that's the divergence — visible as two candles side by side where one clearly breaches a level and the other clearly doesn't.

## Where the two-stage confirmation shows up visually

The first stage is this same divergence, visible on the 4H (or 1H) chart at the level itself. The second stage shows up **one candle later, on a lower timeframe** — often as a "strength switch," where the asset that looked weaker at the first divergence flips to closing in the stronger direction relative to the other asset. Visually this looks like two candles that closed the opposite way from what they did on the previous bar. See [[Example 4 - Gold 2AM Two-Stage PSP Strength Switch]] for exactly what this looks like in practice.

\# What Creates a C2

← [[Combining them]]

## The mechanism

C2 is created when price **sweeps C1's level** — trades beyond C1's low or high — and then **closes back inside the range**, reclaiming that level rather than sustaining the break. This is the reversal candle: it hits a key level (C1's) and produces a rejection.

This is exactly the [[Reversal Profile Logic|reversal profile]] mechanism from [[4H Profiling]], described here at the candle-formation level: a wick beyond the reference level, followed by a close back inside it.

## What makes it a *valid* C2, not noise

Sweeping a level and closing back inside it happens constantly — most of those instances are meaningless. What turns a sweep into a real C2 is:

1. **The level being swept is a valid C1** — real separation from neighboring swings, not a failure swing (see [[What Creates a C1]]).
2. **SMT confirms the sweep as false** — a correlated asset fails to make the same sweep. This is the core [[SMT Confirmation Rule]] from [[4H Profiling]], and here it needs to arrive in two stages — see [[Two-Stage SMT for the Reversal Candle]].
3. **The wick itself is proportionate** — see [[Wick Size Rule]]. A small wick suggests there's still room for C2 to expand on its own; a large wick suggests most of the available move already happened forming the wick.

## Why C2 is the pivot of the whole framework

Everything upstream (identifying a valid C1) and everything downstream (whether C3 forms and how you'd trade it) depends on whether C2 actually qualifies. A C2 that sweeps a failure swing, or that has no SMT, isn't a real reversal — it's just price continuing to test noise, and the "continuation" that would follow it isn't a real C3 either.

## Related
- [[What C2 Looks Like on the Chart]]
- [[Trading Requirements for C2]]
- [[Two-Stage SMT for the Reversal Candle]]

\# Trading Requirements for C3

← [[Combining them]] · See also [[What Creates a C3]]

## Standard requirements

1. **C2 must already be a confirmed reversal** — see [[Trading Requirements for C2]] (requirement set 1, at minimum).
2. **A gap must be present** inside the correct half of C2's wick.
3. Price must **tap into that gap**, with **SMT** confirming the tap.
4. Preferred execution timeframe is **1H or 30M** — not 15M. See [[Why 30M and 1H, Not 15M]].

Meeting these four is the normal, highest-quality version of a C3 entry — see [[The Wick-in-Gap Alignment Setup]] and [[Example 1 - RTY YM 6AM Reversal 1H Gap]].

## If there's no gap

Don't default to trading C3 anyway. There are exactly two narrow exceptions where a gap-less entry is still acceptable, and neither of them is "on C3" in the usual sense:

- [[Regular Swing Point Rule (Only Inside C2)]] — a valid gap-less swing can be traded, but only if it forms **inside C2**, not C3.
- [[90-Minute Cracking Correlation]] — the true last resort: drop to a 90-minute chart for a cracking-correlation SMT, then execute on 5M/3M.

Outside of those two cases, no gap generally means no trade.

## The "already expanding" case

If C3 opened and is already expanding with no wick/gap to react to (see [[Simultaneous C3 Across Timeframes (No Swing Forms)]]), the requirement shifts: position immediately using lower-timeframe order flow around the EQ of the prior range, rather than waiting for a gap that isn't going to form.

## Related

\# What C3 Looks Like on the Chart

← [[Combining them]] · See also [[What Creates a C3]]

## The standard pattern

On the 1H or 30M chart, directly underneath the 4H C3 candle:

- A small wick that sits **inside C2's wick**, specifically in the half that corresponds to the continuation direction (upper half of C2's wick if you're expecting price to go up, lower half if down).
- A **gap** visible inside that same zone.
- Price **opens, dips into the gap, and then expands away from it** — visually a small pullback/retest immediately followed by a strong directional push.
- SMT visible at the same moment: a correlated asset either fails to tap as deep into the gap, or diverges in some equivalent way.

## The "immediate expansion" variant

Sometimes there's no retest to look at all: the candle opens with a **tiny wick** and just expands straight away. This is visually distinct — no clean pullback, no obvious gap tap, just a small flicker at the open followed by continuous directional movement. This version is recognizable *before* it happens by checking whether 4H, 1H, and 30M are all opening a fresh C3 at the same time, and by measuring the EQ of the prior range as the expected reaction zone. See [[Simultaneous C3 Across Timeframes (No Swing Forms)]].

## What "no valid C3" looks like

If C2 didn't leave a gap, and C3 opens without creating one of its own, you'll typically see price just run through prior swing points without ever pausing to retest — this is the visual tell that there's nothing to trade here in the standard way (see [[Trading Requirements for C3]] for the narrow exceptions).

\# What Creates a C3

← [[Combining them]]

## The mechanism

C3 is created by the market **delivering on the expectation C2 set up** — per [[Reversal Profile Logic]], once a candle reverses, the next candle is assumed to continue in that direction. C3 is that next candle actually doing it.

Mechanically, on the lower timeframe, C3 forms by:

1. Opening.
2. Creating a small wick that dips back into the **upper or lower half of C2's own wick** (upper half for a bullish continuation, lower half for bearish) — see [[The Wick-in-Gap Alignment Setup]].
3. Tapping into a **gap** that sits inside that zone.
4. Expanding away from it, with SMT confirming the tap.

## The other way C3 gets created: no new base at all

Sometimes C3 doesn't build a fresh wick/gap at all — it just opens and expands immediately. This happens when there is **already an existing swing structure on every relevant timeframe** (4H, 1H, 30M) before the new candle opens. In that case the market doesn't need to create new structure to continue — it already has the structure it needs, and C3 is just that continuation being delivered without a pause. See [[Simultaneous C3 Across Timeframes (No Swing Forms)]].

## Why C3 needs a gap (normally)

Without a gap, there's no defined zone for price to retest before continuing — which means C3 could just as easily run straight through any candidate entry point instead of giving you a clean re-entry. That's why, absent a gap, C3 is largely **not traded** except through the two narrow exceptions in [[Regular Swing Point Rule (Only Inside C2)]] and [[90-Minute Cracking Correlation]].

\# "Missed C1" — Identifying the Real Reference Level

← [[Combining them]]

## You can't actually miss C1

Since [[Trading Requirements for C1|C1 was never a trade]] in the first place, there's nothing to "miss" — no entry existed there to catch. What people actually mean when they feel like they "missed C1" is that they **misidentified which level was the real reference**, and only realized it after price had already reacted to a different one.

## The real failure mode

The common mistake is anchoring to a level that's too close to other recent swings — a failure swing rather than a genuinely relevant one (see [[What Creates a C1]]). If you're watching a cluster of tightly-packed highs expecting a reversal off any one of them, you'll be constantly wrong-footed, because price tends to run straight through failure swings and only reacts meaningfully at the level with real separation.

## How to get back onside

1. Zoom out and re-identify the **actual** relevant level — the one with real distance from neighboring swings, not the nearest one.
2. Check whether price has already reacted to that real level. If a candle already swept it and closed back inside the range with SMT, you're not looking at a missed C1 at all — you're looking at an already-confirmed C2. Move straight to [[Trading Requirements for C2]] and, if you're too late for C2 itself, to [[Missed C2 - Getting Onside at C3]].
3. If price hasn't reached the real level yet, you haven't missed anything — you were just watching the wrong reference. Reset your attention to the correct level and wait.

\# "Missed C2" — Getting Onside at C3

← [[Combining them]]

## This is the real, common miss

Unlike C1, C2 genuinely can be traded (see [[Trading Requirements for C2]]) — so missing it is a real thing that happens: the reversal candle closes, SMT confirms it, and you weren't positioned. The good news: the framework is explicitly built around the assumption that this happens often, and C3 exists as the designed recovery path, not an afterthought.

## The recovery path

1. **Confirm C2 actually qualifies** — key level hit, SMT present (see [[What Creates a C2]]). If it doesn't, there's no reversal to expect continuation from at all, and there's nothing to "catch."
2. **Drop to the 1H or 30M chart** and wait for C3 to form its own setup: a wick inside the correct half of C2's wick, tapping a gap, confirmed by SMT. See [[What C3 Looks Like on the Chart]] and [[The Wick-in-Gap Alignment Setup]].
3. **Check how much time is left in C2** if you're tempted to jump in immediately rather than wait for C3 — see [[Time Remaining in C2 - The Core Decision Tree]]. With enough time left, you may still be able to catch continuation inside C2 itself rather than waiting all the way for C3.
4. **If there's no gap at all**, check the two narrow fallbacks before giving up: [[Regular Swing Point Rule (Only Inside C2)]] (only valid if the swing is inside C2, not C3) and, as a last resort, [[90-Minute Cracking Correlation]].
5. **If 4H, 1H, and 30M are all opening a fresh C3 simultaneously** with an existing swing already in place, don't wait for a gap that isn't coming — see [[Simultaneous C3 Across Timeframes (No Swing Forms)]] and position immediately.

## The mindset

Missing C2 is not missing the trade — C2 is confirmation, C3 is the entry. The framework treats C3 as the primary, expected entry point precisely because C2 is so often unavailable (large wick, single-stage SMT only, or simply already closed by the time you looked). Chasing C2 after the fact is the wrong instinct; waiting for C3 to build its own qualifying setup is the correct one.

\# The Fractal Chain — C3 Becomes the Next C1

← [[Combining them]]

## The key insight

C1/C2/C3 is not a one-time pattern that happens once a day and then is done. It's a **rolling triplet** that slides forward through the entire [[4H Session Map|4H session chain]] — 18:00 → 22:00 → 02:00 → 06:00 → 10:00. Whichever candle just continued a reversal (C3) becomes the reference level (C1) for whatever reversal forms next.

## How this maps onto the 4H chain

Take the [[Reversal Profile Logic]] chain directly:

| If the triplet is... | Then... |
|---|---|
| 18:00 (C1) → 22:00 (C2) → 02:00 (C3) | 22:00 reverses away from 18:00's level; 02:00 continues |
| 22:00 (C1) → 02:00 (C2) → 06:00 (C3) | 02:00 reverses away from 22:00's level; 06:00 continues |
| 02:00 (C1) → 06:00 (C2) → 10:00 (C3) | 06:00 reverses away from 02:00's level; 10:00 continues |

Notice 02:00 and 06:00 each appear twice — once as C3 for the previous triplet, once as C1 or C2 for the next. That's the fractal part: the same candle can finish one role and immediately start the next.

## Why this matters practically

If you're waiting on a 10:00 continuation, you don't need to go back all the way to 18:00 to find your reference level — the relevant C1 is likely just [[0600 Reversal|06:00]] or [[0200 Reversal|02:00]], whichever one is closest and still structurally relevant. Always ask "which candle is actually playing C1 for the setup I'm looking at right now" rather than assuming it's fixed to a specific time of day.

\# Timestamp Reference Sheet

← [[Combining them]]

Two layers of timestamps matter in this framework: the **4H chain** (which candle is C1/C2/C3 right now) and the **intra-candle driver times** (where inside a 4H candle the actual LTF entry tends to land). All times NY local, matching [[4H Session Map]].

## Layer 1 — The 4H chain (which candle is which)

The triplet slides forward one candle at a time — see [[The Fractal Chain (C3 Becomes the Next C1)]].

| Time | Candle | Typically plays... |
|---|---|---|
| 18:00 | Daily open | C1 for the 18:00→22:00→02:00 triplet |
| 22:00 | 10pm | C2 of that triplet, or C1 of the next |
| 02:00 | 2am | C3 of the first triplet, C2 or C1 of the next |
| 06:00 | 6am | C3 or C2, depending on which reversal is live |
| 10:00 | 10am | Usually C3 — the primary NY continuation candle |
| 14:00 | 2pm | Not used — see [[1400 - No Trade]] |

## Layer 2 — Where inside the candle the entry actually lands

This is the part governed by [[Time Remaining in C2 - The Core Decision Tree]] — how much of the current 4H candle is left changes what you're looking for. Times pulled directly from the worked examples:

| 4H candle window | Observed LTF reaction time | What happened there | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10:00–14:00 | **11:00** | Price taps the 1H gap with SMT — the aligned entry | [[Example 1 - RTY YM 6AM Reversal 1H Gap]] |
| 06:00–10:00 | **9:00** | Strength-switch PSP confirms a protected low despite no clean reversal close | [[Example 4 - Gold 2AM Two-Stage PSP Strength Switch]] |
| 06:00–10:00 | **9:30** (driver) | NY cash-open driver delivers price closer to the draw, regardless of time left | [[Example 5 - Gold Driver 930 Continuation in C2]] |
| 06:00–10:00 | **10:00** | Finishes the move to the draw on liquidity | [[Example 5 - Gold Driver 930 Continuation in C2]] |
| 06:00–10:00 | **8:30** | Strength-switch SMT confirms continuation toward the highs, ~1.5 hrs still left in the candle | [[Example 6 - Gold C2 Continuation With Time Left]] |
| 06:00–10:00 | **7:00 / 8:00** | 07:00 candle's SMT divergence confirms the aligned 1H swing; delivery follows at 08:00 | [[Example 7 - Continuation Equal Highs 1H Swing in Gap]] |

## How to use this in practice

1. Identify which 4H candle you're in and what role it's playing (Layer 1).
2. Apply [[Time Remaining in C2 - The Core Decision Tree]]: how much of that candle is left right now?
3. If a **driver** (9:30 is the one explicitly named in this framework) falls within the remaining window, expect it to matter regardless of the clock — see [[Drivers - The Time Exception]].
4. Watch the specific top-of-hour / half-hour marks (like 8:30, 9:00, 9:30) as the recurring moments where SMT/strength-switch confirmations tend to actually land, based on the pattern across the worked examples above.

\# C1 / C2 / C3 Framework

Central hub for the three-candle model used throughout [[4H Profiling]] and [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]]. Every reversal-into-continuation setup in this vault is really just this triplet, sliding forward through the day one candle at a time.

> This model also extends to a **C4** case, and sits inside a much deeper full treatment — see [[Candle Profiling - Complete Framework]] for the complete version, including [[When C2 and C3 Both Fail to Manipulate (The C4 Case)]].

## The one-sentence version

> C1 sets the level, C2 sweeps it and reverses, C3 continues — and each one has its own separate, non-interchangeable requirements before it's tradable.

## The three candles, at a glance

| | Role | Tradable on its own? | Core requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1** | Establishes the reference level (a low or high) | No — it's a reference, not a signal | Must be a **relevant** level, not a failure swing |
| **C2** | Sweeps C1's level and reverses, closing back inside the range | Sometimes — only with enough confirmation | [[Two-Stage SMT for the Reversal Candle\|Two-stage SMT]] + small wick + time left in the candle |
| **C3** | Continues C2's reversal | Yes — this is the primary entry candle | Gap inside the correct half of C2's wick + SMT confirming the tap |

## Go deep on each candle

**C1 — The Origin Candle**
- [[What Creates a C1]]
- [[What C1 Looks Like on the Chart]]
- [[Trading Requirements for C1]]

**C2 — The Reversal Candle**
- [[What Creates a C2]]
- [[What C2 Looks Like on the Chart]]
- [[Trading Requirements for C2]]

**C3 — The Continuation Candle**
- [[What Creates a C3]]
- [[What C3 Looks Like on the Chart]]
- [[Trading Requirements for C3]]

## Bringing it back together

You can't trade all three — by the time C3 is forming, C1 is old news and C2 may already be closed. The real skill is knowing **which candle you're currently able to act on**, and how to get onside if you missed an earlier one.

- [[The Fractal Chain (C3 Becomes the Next C1)]] — why this triplet isn't a one-time pattern, it repeats all day
- [[Missed C1 - Identifying the Real Reference Level]] — you can't actually "miss" C1 (nothing to trade), but you can misidentify it
- [[Missed C2 - Getting Onside at C3]] — the real recovery path when you miss the reversal candle
- [[Timestamp Reference Sheet]] — how this triplet maps onto actual clock times, both the 4H chain and the intra-candle driver times

## Related
- [[4H Profiling]] — the HTF chain this triplet is built from (see [[Reversal Profile Logic]])
- [[1H-30M Alignment to 4H Profile]] — the LTF execution layer that trades C2/C3 in practice

\# C2 Closures That Support vs. Don't Support Expansion

← [[Candle Profiling - Complete Framework]]

## The base case: C2 sweeps C1's low/high

A C2 candle comes and sweeps C1's low (bullish case) or high (bearish case), then closes back above/below that wick. That closure itself is not automatically tradable — what determines whether it is comes down to **wick size**.

## Case 1 — Large wick: does not support expansion

If C2's wick is large relative to the move, **don't trade this candle.** Let it close, and plan to trade **C3** instead. A large wick means the candle already used up most of the available range just forming the rejection — there isn't enough left in it to also expand.

This applies symmetrically:
- Bullish scenario: C2 sweeps C1's low with a large wick, closes back above it — still don't trade C2, wait for C3.
- Bearish scenario: C2 sweeps C1's high with a large wick, closes back below it — same treatment, wait for C3.

## Case 2 — Small wick: supports expansion (reversal-to-expansion candle)

If C2 has an **extremely small wick** and a small opposing run, it supports expansion on its own — this is the "C2 reversal-to-expansion" candle. You can trade this candle directly, in the direction of the reversal:
- C2 sweeps C1's high, reverses lower with a small wick → tradable lower.
- C2 sweeps C1's low, reverses higher with a small wick → tradable higher.

## Case 3 — Neither C2 nor C3 manipulates a prior wick

Sometimes there's no clean sweep of a previous wick by either C2 or C3, but a candle still closes **above C2's own wick high** (or below its low), showing willingness and a reversal signature on its own. This is treated as valid too — the reversal signature itself (closing beyond the prior candle's wick) substitutes for a direct sweep. This is the doorway into [[When C2 and C3 Both Fail to Manipulate (The C4 Case)]].

\# The Two Non-Negotiables — Key Level and Open Draw

← [[Candle Profiling - Complete Framework]]

## The rule, stated directly

**There is no profile — none — without both of these being true:**

1. A **key level** was taken (manipulated/swept) prior to the reversal or continuation you're looking at.
2. There is an **open draw** — an unmet liquidity target still sitting out there for price to reach.

Every single example in this framework assumes both of these are already in place. If either one is missing, there's nothing to trade — not a weak setup, not a lower-probability setup, *nothing*.

## Why this is stated so absolutely

It's tempting to treat "key level" and "open draw" as nice-to-haves that improve a setup's quality. They aren't — they're the precondition for the setup existing at all. A candle that reverses without having taken a real key level first isn't a profile, it's noise that happened to look like one. A reversal with no open draw left to reach has nowhere to send you, so there's no trade to plan even if the reversal itself looks clean.

## How to apply this as a filter

Before analyzing anything else about a candle — its wick size, its closure, its alignment across timeframes — ask these two questions first:

1. Did price actually take a key level here, or is this candle just moving?
2. Is there liquidity left unmet that this move could be heading toward?

If either answer is no, stop. Don't keep analyzing wick shape or SMT on a candle that fails this first filter — nothing downstream can rescue a setup that doesn't have both of these.

\# What Is Candle Profiling

← [[Candle Profiling - Complete Framework]]

## The core definition

Candle profiling is a road map for the day, built candle by candle from the **closure behavior** of the candles that come before it. Its foundation is the **C2 and C3 closure** — how a candle closes relative to the level it just swept determines whether you have a tradable profile at all.

## Why it matters

Profiling is your guideline for the session: it tells you, before price has fully committed, what kind of day you're likely looking at (a reversal day, a continuation day, a straight expansion) and which candle is likely to be the one that matters. Without it, you're reacting to individual candles with no larger structure to judge them against.

## The starting point: C2 closures

Everything downstream — [[The Two Non-Negotiables (Key Level and Open Draw)|key levels and open draws]], [[Two-Stage Cracks for Reversals|SMT]], [[The Fractal Alignment Filter (Daily, 4H, 1H)|fractal alignment]] — sits on top of this one basic read: did the candle that just swept a level close in a way that **supports further expansion**, or not? See [[C2 Closures That Support vs Don't Support Expansion]].

\# When C2 and C3 Both Fail to Manipulate — The C4 Case

← [[Candle Profiling - Complete Framework]] · See also [[C2 Closures That Support vs Don't Support Expansion]]

## The situation

Sometimes neither C2 nor C3 cleanly manipulates a previous wick or key level in the way [[Combining them|the standard triplet]] expects. Instead:

- C2 has a large wick and doesn't support expansion (see [[C2 Closures That Support vs Don't Support Expansion]]) — you already know not to trade it.
- C3, rather than delivering a clean continuation off C2, is itself the candle that finally **closes beyond C2's wick high (or low)**, showing a genuine reversal signature for the first time.

Because the "real" reversal signature didn't show up until C3, the continuation you're now waiting for shifts one candle later — onto what this framework labels **C4**.

## Why this extends the model

[[Combining them]] treats C2 as the reversal and C3 as the continuation. This is the case where that assignment doesn't hold cleanly — C2 fails to qualify, and the reversal role effectively slides onto C3 instead. The continuation candle you're actually trading is then the one after that: C4.

## How to trade it

The execution method doesn't change — it's the same [[The Refined Key Level and the 50% Open Rule|refined key level]] mechanic used for any continuation candle. You're just applying it one candle later in the sequence than usual, because the qualifying reversal signature took longer to show up. See [[Example 4 - C4 Continuation After Invalid C2 and C3]] for the full worked case.
